A SCORING MACHINE.

Putting up 25 points per game in the NBA requires elite scoring ability. Doing it season after season, for more than a decade, puts you in a completely different category.

LeBron James leads NBA history with an incredible 20 seasons, averaging at least 25 points per game.

Kevin Durant is right behind him with 17 seasons, while Kobe Bryant, Karl Malone, and Michael Jordan each recorded 12 seasons at the 25+ PPG mark. 🐐

🔸 LeBron James: 20 seasons
🔸 Kevin Durant: 17 seasons
🔸 Kobe Bryant: 12 seasons
🔸 Karl Malone: 12 seasons
🔸 Michael Jordan: 12 seasons

From LeBron's unmatched longevity to Durant's scoring consistency and the dominance of Kobe, Malone, and Jordan, these numbers show just how difficult it is to remain an elite scorer year after year.

25 PPG isn't just a scoring milestone; maintaining it across multiple seasons is a testament to consistency, durability, and offensive greatness 🏀🔥
